subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the macOS Dashboard browser inject only configured shared gateway tokens, or may it reuse native/operator device tokens for browser Control UI auth parity?
rationale: The PR, linked bug, docs, and sibling PR encode two incompatible auth-boundary choices; automation can identify the conflict but cannot choose the product/security policy for existing users.

options.title: Use shared-token-only browser injection
options.body: Treat native device tokens as native-client credentials only, update every Dashboard browser auth path to inject shared token/password or no token, and close the conflicting native-token parity direction.

options.title: Allow native/operator parity
options.body: Keep native device token fallback for the embedded Dashboard and close or retarget this shared-token-only PR as the wrong boundary.

options.title: Pause both branches for an auth design note
options.body: Keep both PRs unmerged until maintainers document when browser Control UI may receive shared secrets, passwords, identity headers, or device tokens.

recommendation.title: Use shared-token-only browser injection
recommendation.body: Treat native device tokens as native-client credentials only, update every Dashboard browser auth path to inject shared token/password or no token, and close the conflicting native-token parity direction.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and recently changed the central Dashboard auth paths, including the current-main endpoint observer that this PR now must reconcile.
